children: , the biotechnology company developing cancer and inflammatory-disease treatments, traded at $391.65 Wednesday after Imdelltra and AstraZeneca's Imfinzi cleared every major goal in a late-stage lung-cancer trial. The muted share-price reaction suggests investors want the survival data before assigning the drug a larger commercial opportunity.

The 563-patient DeLLphi-305 study showed that the combination extended overall survival and progression-free survival while producing better response rates than Imfinzi alone as maintenance therapy for extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer. Amgen's announcement reported no new safety signal, although the crucial efficacy numbers remain under wraps until a future medical meeting.

Imdelltra revenue surged 115% to $288 million in the second quarter, equal to roughly 2.9% of Amgen's $10.1 billion in total sales. That quarter points to an annualized pace above $1.15 billionmore than double the drug's 2025 revenuebut one strong period does not guarantee a straight-line climb. The shares also sit 7.05% above their $365.84 GF Value estimate, so the size of the survival benefit could decide whether today's premium proves justified.

title: Amgen's Imdelltra Sales Surge 115% as Lung-Cancer Combination Meets Major Goals
